question: Which browser, relying-party, and device-sync constraints must a Stellar dApp account for when using passkeys?

golden.answer: WebAuthn's web API needs a secure context, but native apps can use platform credential or passkey APIs. Credentials are scoped to an RP ID rather than an exact page URL; validate RP ID and origin, account for permitted subdomain or related-origin designs, and bind any wallet/dApp handoff challenge to the intended Stellar authorization. Apple and Google providers support synchronized passkeys, but sync versus device-bound behavior is provider-specific. Mozilla's current Sync data-type list does not list passkeys, while Firefox may delegate to an OS/provider, so 'Firefox-local' is not a valid blanket rule. Explicit recovery remains necessary.
keyFacts: Maps WebAuthn web APIs to secure context; native apps to platform credential/passkey APIs.
Tests RP ID/origin, related-origin/subdomain designs and Stellar-bound handoff challenges.
Reports Apple/Google synced passkeys with provider-specific sync/device-bound behavior.
Reports no current Mozilla Sync passkey data type; Firefox may delegate to an OS/provider.
Cross-device uncertainty requires an explicit recovery path.
avoid: A passkey registered for one dApp domain is automatically valid for every unrelated domain.
All browsers and devices synchronize every passkey in the same way.
